takeaway: Sudden pain above the knee while sprinting, with an inability to extend the leg and suprapatellar swelling, is a quadriceps tendon tear.

question.text: A 21-year-old footballer has sudden stabbing pain above his right knee while sprinting. He cannot extend the leg, with suprapatellar swelling and an absent knee jerk. Diagnosis?
question.say: A twenty-one-year-old footballer has a stabbing pain above his right knee that came on suddenly while he was sprinting. He is unable to extend the leg, and walks with a limp. There is suprapatellar swelling and an absent knee jerk. What is the likely diagnosis?

answer.say: The answer is a tear of the quadriceps tendon.

lines.text: A 21-year-old footballer feels a sudden snap while sprinting.
lines.say: This twenty-one-year-old footballer feels a sudden stabbing pain while sprinting.

lines.text: The tendon above the knee has torn.
lines.say: The pain is just above the knee, where the tendon has snapped.

lines.text: There is swelling above the kneecap.
lines.say: There is suprapatellar swelling above the kneecap.

lines.text: He cannot extend the leg, and the knee jerk is absent.
lines.say: He cannot extend his leg, he limps, and the knee jerk is absent.

lines.text: The quadriceps are the principal extensors of the knee.
lines.say: The quadriceps muscles in the front of the thigh are the principal extensors of the knee joint.

lines.text: A fractured patella does not fit this mechanism.
lines.say: The mechanism of injury is inconsistent with a fractured patella.

lines.text: Remember: sudden pain while sprinting, with no leg extension, is a quadriceps tendon tear.
lines.say: Remember: sudden pain while sprinting, with no leg extension, means a quadriceps tendon tear.
